source.title: Reward prediction error signaling in posterior dorsomedial striatum is action specific

confidence_rationale: Single-unit rat evidence that RPE-like teaching signals in posterior dorsomedial striatum (pDMS) are ACTION-SPECIFIC -- unlike midbrain dopamine RPEs, which are not. This localises the INFORMATIVE action-critic teaching signal that REE's actor-critic pathway would need, and shows it is a distinct, action-addressed channel whose absence would specifically impair action-value updating. Confidence 0.58: the population is small (10% of pDMS fast-firing neurons), the species is rodent, and the link to active competence LOSS is inferential -- the paper shows the signal's existence and specificity, not the consequence of removing it.
failure_signatures: The action-specific RPE population was only ~10% of pDMS fast-firing neurons (19/196) -- a thin substrate, so arguments that its uninformativeness dominates behaviour must be careful about how much of the action-value teaching signal it actually carries.

Midbrain dopamine RPEs are explicitly NOT action-specific; if REE's critic teaching signal is modelled on a global DA-like RPE rather than this pDMS action-addressed signal, the biological analog for an informative action-critic is mis-specified -- a design caveat, not support.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In rats whose action-reward predictions were repeatedly violated, a subpopulation of fast-firing neurons in posterior dorsomedial striatum (19/196, ~10%) showed RPE-like activity -- phasic increases to unexpected reward, decreases to unexpected omission -- that, unlike midbrain dopamine RPEs, was ACTION-SPECIFIC (tied to the animal's anti-preferred action), providing a mechanism to update action-specific representations.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-475 says REE's critic is uninformative on the policy's own state distribution, so the action-value advantage carries variance not signal. This paper identifies the biological teaching signal that a WELL-FORMED action-critic uses -- an action-specific RPE in dorsomedial striatum -- distinct from the global, non-action-specific dopamine RPE. It reinforces the Samejima/Rothenhoefer resolution: the informative critic REE lacks is an action-addressed signal in dorsal striatum, and a flat/global critic is precisely the failure mode where such action-specific credit is absent.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Rodent single-unit correlational data; the action-specific RPE population is small and the paper demonstrates the signal's EXISTENCE and specificity, not that its loss causes competence to fall below control. The causal/destructive step for MECH-475 is carried by the lesion and computational entries; this entry grounds the LOCUS and FORM of the informative teaching signal only.
mapping.source_context: Extracellular recording of fast-firing and phasically-firing neurons (n=1076) in posterior dorsomedial and dorsolateral striatum of rats during repeated violation of action-reward predictions.

confidence_components.notes: Solid J Neurosci single-unit study; mapping_fidelity 0.55 (locus/form of the teaching signal, not the destructive consequence); transfer_risk 0.5 for rodent -> REE. Complements Samejima on the same locus question from the RPE/teaching-signal side.
